name: Erik Hansen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no employer or AI-company ties. Your answers stay confidential. Tell me about an ordinary day at work.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am forty-three and lead the cooperative accounts desk at North Quay Accounts, so I check grant entries, review returns and call volunteer treasurers when a bank line makes no sense. I enjoy the call when the books finally click for someone; the repeated hunt for a missing bank page wears me out. My partner and I have two school-age children, and one of us is usually looking at tomorrow's pickup while I finish a file.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How did you get into that senior role?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I did a master's degree and earned my chartered accountancy qualification, then spent years learning what small cooperatives actually record. I am among the best on this desk, but I still ask another reviewer to challenge a strange grant entry.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau — Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell people at North Quay Accounts that a faster scan of routine receipts is fine as long as a senior accountant still signs the return. Most cooperative treasurers want a person who will explain a strange number.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm paid well for this job and we have more than eight months of bills saved, so I don't see a small software gain threatening my place. Our mortgage still needs paying, and the children are at the age when school trips appear without warning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep checking cooperative tax returns against bank statements and use the hour saved on routine sorting to call the treasurers with open questions. I'd add forty each month from pay to the school-trip pot rather than spend it because the scanner seems clever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own job and income here. I have a buffer and plenty of similar firms nearby if ordinary work ever changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What part of the work do you enjoy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: When a volunteer treasurer understands why the books finally balance, I feel I've done something useful. Chasing a missing bank page for a week is the tiresome part.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you use AI yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now and then I ask an approved tool to sort a long query list, then check the original entries. I wait until a colleague has tested a tool before I use it on a client job.

say: I'd keep a **senior sign-off** on each cooperative tax return.
I'd use the saved time for **treasurer calls** about open questions.
think: My **higher pay** and eight-month buffer make the modest change manageable.
The mortgage and **school trips** still need cash.
do: Keep checking **cooperative tax returns** against original bank statements before signing.
Add **forty monthly** from wages to the children's school-trip pot.
S0.quote: Most cooperative treasurers want a person who will explain a strange number.
fieldNote: His **tested occasional AI use** and original-document checks remain the working routine in a mild scenario.
Higher pay, **eight months saved** and plentiful nearby firms support a calm mood despite the household mortgage.

steps.text: Keep checking cooperative tax returns against original bank statements
Save forty monthly from wages for school trips

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption — Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners to show us the error rate before they give each reviewer twice as many cooperative accounts. A fast return with a wrong grant number is not a saving for the client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The new software could take checking and drafting off my desk, so I may supervise fewer people even if my salary holds. I'm experienced, but I won't claim a master's degree and a chartered qualification protect every paid hour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for two paid sessions to learn the new grant-check screen on closed cooperative files, with another senior reviewing my corrections. In the first year of steady disruption, if North Quay removes a paid day from my week, I'd apply for posted senior accounting roles at nearby firms and keep North Quay paid hours until a written offer gives a mortgage-covering wage and start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a real cut to my own week. The eight-month buffer buys a search, but I don't want to drain it to cover regular bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the partners won't fund the sessions?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd continue with the approved checker and ask them to put the new targets in writing. I would not spend our family savings on mandatory training or test live grant files at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What evidence would persuade you the new screen works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want the missed-grant count and the time it takes to repair each miss, not a slide showing only speed. If that holds across the old files, I'll use it.

say: I'd demand a **missed-grant count** before the partners double each reviewer's target.
I'd accept a **tested screen** only with paid review time on real files.
think: My **paid week** could shrink despite my senior title.
An eight-month buffer is for shocks, not **regular wages**.
do: Learn the **grant screen** on closed files during two approved paid supervised sessions; use only after missed-grant and repair-time checks pass.
Apply for **posted nearby accounting** if North Quay cuts a paid day.
Keep **paid North Quay work** until written mortgage-covering outside terms start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing a paid day.

fieldNote: He will learn a **new grant screen** only during approved paid sessions; refusal sends him back to approved checks.
An actual **lost paid day** triggers local search; a move needs a posted vacancy and written mortgage-covering wage and start.

steps.text: Learn grant screen on closed files during two approved paid sessions with senior review
Use new controls live only after measured errors and repair-time checks pass

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 — Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our cooperative clients full AGI in 2028 can do almost all the thinking in their tax return, and somebody still has to answer for an error. Robots for hands-on work arrive around 2031; they don't give accountants three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: North Quay may cut most review posts, including mine, before I can make a neat plan. The cushion is real, and nearby firms exist, but those firms may cut at the same time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd postpone the kitchen refit and add one hundred from each month's wages to emergency cash now. In the first year after 2028, if my job ends, I'd apply for advertised salaried finance-manager posts at the local housing association, while taking only paid North Quay closeout files still offered until a written bill-covering wage and start date are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect my own high salary could go, not simply a colleague's. Eight months of expenses buys time, not certainty that a housing-association vacancy will open.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the housing association?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Its accounts team handles rent and repair budgets, which I have checked for cooperative clients. Full AGI reaches that desk too, so I'd apply only for an actual paid post, not call it a safe shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children about the refit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my two children we're keeping the kitchen as it is while we protect the mortgage. I would rather give them an honest smaller plan than wait for the savings to vanish.

say: I'd say **2028 thinking work** changes before physical robots around 2031.
I'd require **human accountability** for tax errors.
think: I expect my **senior salary** may disappear quickly if North Quay cuts tax reviews.
Other local firms may face the **same cuts** when full AGI reaches accounting work.
do: Postpone the **kitchen refit** and save one hundred monthly from wages.
Apply for **posted housing finance** after losing my post.
Keep **paid closeout files** while offered until written bill-covering terms start.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing my salary.
S2.quote: Eight months of expenses buys time, not certainty that a housing-association vacancy will open.
fieldNote: His higher pay means a lost post removes **substantial household income**, even with a strong cushion and many nearby firms.
Postponing the refit adds **new cash monthly** from wages; housing-association work needs an advertised salaried vacancy and written bill-covering terms.

steps.text: Postpone kitchen refit and save one hundred monthly from wages

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031 — Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners five years is enough to count which cooperative reviews clients still pay for. Full AGI reaches our desk in 2031, while robots for physical work come around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could pay down the mortgage and still need a wage when I'm 48. Nearby firms give me options, but their tax work is exposed too, so I won't assume a different sign on the door solves it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd put one hundred a month from our current wages against the mortgage and ask North Quay for annual figures on paid grant reviews. In the first year after 2031, if the firm cannot fund my senior salary from that work, I'd apply for posted salaried housing-finance posts and keep any paid North Quay work while offered until a written bill-covering wage and start date are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about whether the wage survives, though I have more time than in the 2028 picture. A smaller mortgage would give us more room to refuse a poor offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a course before 2031?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I already have a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I'd take a housing-budget module only if a posted paid association role requires it and the employer funds both fee and paid study time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if that employer won't fund it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd skip the module and keep earning at North Quay while work is available. A course paid from our buffer is a bet on a vacancy that may never appear.

say: I'd ask for **paid grant-review figures** from North Quay each year.
I'd distinguish **2031 desk exposure** from 2034 physical robots at clients' sites.
think: A nearby firm may face **similar tax pressure** when AGI reaches the accounts desk.
A smaller mortgage would let me **reject weak pay** from a new employer.
do: Pay **one hundred monthly** off the mortgage; request annual paid grant-review figures from North Quay.
Take a **funded housing module** only for a posted paid role.
Apply for **posted housing finance** if senior pay is unfunded; retain offered North Quay work until written bill-covering wage/start.
S3.quote: A course paid from our buffer is a bet on a vacancy that may never appear.
fieldNote: His five-year plan uses **current pay** to lower debt and paid-review figures to test whether salary remains supportable.
The module needs **funded fees** and paid study time for a posted role; he keeps offered North Quay pay until written terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036 — Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade is enough to stop treating a high salary as a permanent fact. Full AGI reaches tax reasoning in 2036; robots for site work may follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I'd still have the mortgage unless we pay it down deliberately. I enjoy the cooperative clients. I cannot retire on a good reputation if review fees no longer fund my salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd pay an extra one hundred and twenty monthly off the mortgage while both household wages hold, then ask the partners each tax season for the paid-review renewal figures. In the first year after 2036, if North Quay cannot fund my senior salary from those fees, I'd apply for posted salaried housing-finance work and keep any paid firm hours while offered until a written bill-covering wage and start date are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about needing work at 53, even with more than six months saved today. A decade lets us prepare, but the desk still changes on the AGI date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If your partner's pay falls before then?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd stop the extra mortgage payment and use current cash for essentials. The ordinary instalment and children's needs come before a tidy early-payoff plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave now to get ahead?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. North Quay pays me well and the client work is there today; I would check the renewals rather than abandon a current wage for a possibility.

I'd explain **2036 desk change** ahead of 2039 site robots.
think: My **reputation** may not fund a salary at 53 after client review fees disappear.
The mortgage needs **actual paid work** even if we have saved for years.
do: Pay **120 extra monthly** off the mortgage while both wages hold; stop and use cash for essentials if partner pay falls.
Apply for **posted housing finance** if renewal fees cannot fund senior pay; retain offered firm work until written bill-covering wage/start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a later wage gap.
S4.quote: I cannot retire on a good reputation if review fees no longer fund my salary.
fieldNote: His extra debt payment depends on **both wages** and stops if his partner's pay falls.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my salary could vanish before we lower the mortgage. A long notice period and a real posted housing-finance vacancy with written pay and start would help more than a general promise of retraining.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what clients will still pay a person to check. A job title can stay on the chart after its paid hours have gone.

headlineQuote: A job title can stay on the chart after its paid hours have gone.
portrait: Erik leads **cooperative tax reviews** at North Quay and likes helping volunteer treasurers untangle accounts.
He uses AI **occasionally** after testing and keeps original bank records in view.
Higher pay, **eight months saved**, nearby firms and two children shape his mortgage choices.
He learns new controls on **approved paid time** and searches only when funded hours or salary fail.
AGI can remove his **senior salary** in 2028; longer warning supports debt reduction.
biggestWorry: He worries most about **AGI by 2028** ending his senior wage before the mortgage falls.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **long notice** and a posted paid housing-finance role with written wage and start.
